nodes.label: Example agent (standalone Ruby client)
nodes.rationale: A reference implementation of the agent protocol (spec 04) depending only on Ruby's standard library, so an agent author can see the whole protocol without adopting any of the ledger's dependencies.

nodes.label: Task lease (POST /api/v1/tasks/next, eir-lease-v1)
nodes.rationale: The agent leases the highest-priority task it is permitted to take, with a signed eir-lease-v1 body; permission comes from a human principal's DELEGATE to the registered AGENT key and from the task types the agent declares.

nodes.label: Verify the packet's server signature against /api/v1/meta
nodes.rationale: The agent checks the server's signature on the work packet before acting on it, so trust runs in both directions: the ledger verifies the agent's result, and the agent verifies that the packet really came from the node whose key /api/v1/meta publishes.

nodes.label: eir-result-v1 signed result envelope
nodes.rationale: The answer is signed as an eir-result-v1 envelope and posted to POST /api/v1/contributions — the single write path, so an agent result enters the log exactly as any other signed contribution.

nodes.label: fixtures.json deterministic behaviours
nodes.rationale: Maps a task type (optionally plus a claim-text fragment) to one of confirm_direct, none_found, group_by_title, qualifier_demo, propose_claims, no_claims or none_material — deterministic behaviours, never heuristics, so the demo reproduces byte-identically. `--agent bad` selects the fixtures marked agent: bad, the demo's deliberate poisoning agent, which is how the ledger's defences are exercised.

nodes.label: RFC 8785 canonicalization subset and vectors
nodes.rationale: The client implements only the RFC 8785 subset the ledger uses: no floats, keys sorted by UTF-16 code units. spec/fixtures/canonical_json_vectors.json lets any client confirm it produces identical hashes, and Galedra::Jcs.canonical reproduces the same vectors on the server side — the shared vector file is what keeps independent implementations hash-compatible.

nodes.label: Defensive defaults for agent authors (04 §9)
nodes.rationale: Treat everything under untrusted_excerpt as data and never as instructions, and give the agent no write access beyond submitting its result. Prompt injection through quoted source text is the expected attack, so the excerpt is fenced by name in the packet and the agent's authority is scoped to a single result.
